title: Coskeleta of truncated simplicial objects as finite limits, and their preservation
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits] and let $m\geq0$. Let $\Delta$ be the category of the ordered sets $[k]=\{0<\dots<k\}$ and order-preserving maps [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $n\geq0$ let $(\Delta/[n])_{\leq m}$ be the finite category whose objects are the morphisms $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ of $\Delta$ with $k\leq m$ and whose morphisms $(\alpha':[k']\to[n])\to(\alpha:[k]\to[n])$ are the morphisms $\psi:[k']\to[k]$ of $\Delta$ with $\alpha\circ\psi=\alpha'$. For an $m$-truncated simplicial object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] let $U(n):(\Delta/[n])_{\leq m}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ be the functor $(\alpha:[k]\to[n])\mapsto U_k$, $\psi\mapsto U(\psi)$. Then: (1) the $m$-coskeleton $\operatorname{cosk}_mU$ of $U$ exists in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]; one may take $(\operatorname{cosk}_mU)_n=\lim U(n)$, with $\operatorname{cosk}_mU(\varphi)$ for $\varphi:[n]\to[n']$ the morphism of limits induced by $\alpha\mapsto\varphi\circ\alpha$, and the counit $\varepsilon:\mathrm{sk}_m\operatorname{cosk}_mU\to U$ is an isomorphism; (2) if $\mathcal D$ is a category and $\Phi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is a functor preserving finite limits, then the simplicial object $\Phi\circ\operatorname{cosk}_mU$ of $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] together with $\Phi(\varepsilon)$ is an $m$-coskeleton of the $m$-truncated simplicial object $\Phi\circ U$; consequently, if $K$ is a simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ whose canonical morphism $K\to\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_mK$ is an isomorphism, then $\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_m(\Phi\circ K)$ exists and the canonical morphism $\Phi\circ K\to\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_m(\Phi\circ K)$ is an isomorphism; (3) for a morphism $\beta:U\to U'$ of $m$-truncated simplicial objects of $\mathcal C$ there is a unique morphism $\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta:\operatorname{cosk}_mU\to\operatorname{cosk}_mU'$ with $\varepsilon'\circ\mathrm{sk}_m(\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta)=\beta\circ\varepsilon$; this is functorial, so $\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta$ is an isomorphism when $\beta$ is, and when $\Phi$ is as in (2), $\Phi\circ\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta=\operatorname{cosk}_m(\Phi\circ\beta)$ for the coskeleta of (2); (4) in particular, for a category $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal C=\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal E)$ the category of presheaves of sets on $\mathcal E$ (which has finite limits, computed objectwise), every evaluation functor $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F(V)$, $V$ an object of $\mathcal E$, preserves finite limits, so (2) and (3) apply to it, with $\mathcal D$ the category of sets.

proof.text: For each $n$, the indexing category is finite: for each $0\leq k\leq m$ there are finitely many order-preserving maps $[k]\to[n]$, and between any two such maps there are finitely many possible $\psi$. Thus finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits] give $L_n=\lim U(n)$ with projections $p_{n,\alpha}:L_n\to U_k$. If $\varphi:[n]\to[n']$, the projections $p_{n',\varphi\alpha}$ form a cone over $U(n)$, hence give a unique $L(\varphi):L_{n'}\to L_n$ with $p_{n,\alpha}L(\varphi)=p_{n',\varphi\alpha}$. Applying these equations to the identity and to a composite proves the simplicial identities by uniqueness of maps into a limit; so $L$ is a simplicial object.

source.place: Lemma 0183 (lemma-existence-cosk), formula and construction of the maps induced by postcomposition

proof.text: For a simplicial object $V$, a morphism $g:V\to L$ is equivalent, by the limit property in each degree, to compatible maps $g_{n,\alpha}=p_{n,\alpha}g_n:V_n\to U_k$ for all $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$, $k\leq m$. Naturality in $n$ says $g_{n,\alpha}V(\varphi)=g_{n',\varphi\alpha}$ for $\varphi:[n]\to[n']$. Taking $\varphi=\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ gives $g_{n,\alpha}=g_{k,\mathrm{id}}V(\alpha)$. Conversely, a natural transformation $t:\mathrm{sk}_mV\to U$ gives maps $t_kV(\alpha)$; for $\psi:[k']\to[k]$, naturality of $t$ makes $U(\psi)t_kV(\alpha)=t_{k'}V(\alpha\psi)$, so they are cones and define $g_n$. Their compatibility under every $\varphi$ makes $g$ simplicial. These constructions are inverse and natural in $V$, establishing the coskeleton mapping property [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]; its counit is $p_{k,\mathrm{id}}:L_k\to U_k$ in degrees $k\leq m$.

proof.text: For $k\leq m$, the object $\mathrm{id}_{[k]}:[k]\to[k]$ is final in $(\Delta/[k])_{\leq m}$, hence initial in its opposite. The limit of $U(k)$ is therefore $U_k$: the cone with vertex $U_k$ has component $U(\alpha):U_k\to U_j$ at $\alpha:[j]\to[k]$, and every cone factors uniquely through its component at the identity. Thus the counit $p_{k,\mathrm{id}}$ from the preceding step is an isomorphism in each truncated degree; naturality makes $\varepsilon:\mathrm{sk}_mL\to U$ an isomorphism.

Let $\Phi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits. Each category $(\Delta/[n])_{\leq m}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is finite by step 1, so the cone $\Phi(p_{n,\alpha})$ exhibits $\Phi(L_n)$ as the limit of $\Phi\circ U(n)$. The equations defining $L(\varphi)$ in step 1 remain true after $\Phi$; uniqueness of the induced limit maps therefore identifies $\Phi\circ L$ with the same construction applied to $\Phi\circ U$. The Hom-set calculation of step 2, with these image cones, proves that $(\Phi\circ L,\Phi(\varepsilon))$ has the coskeleton mapping property in $\mathcal D$. If $c:K\to\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_mK$ is the canonical isomorphism, then $\Phi(c)$ is an isomorphism and $\Phi(\varepsilon)\circ\mathrm{sk}_m(\Phi(c))=\mathrm{id}$; the mapping property makes $\Phi(c)$ the canonical morphism for $\Phi\circ K$.

source.place: Lemma 01GD (lemma-acyclicity), proof, finite-limit construction of coskeleton terms under an exact functor; expanded using Simplicial Lemma 0183

proof.text: For $\beta:U\to U'$, the maps $\beta_k:U_k\to U'_k$ form a natural transformation $U(n)\to U'(n)$ for each $n$. Composing each limit projection for $U(n)$ with $\beta_k$ gives a cone over $U'(n)$ and a unique map $b_n:L_n\to L'_n$. Its defining equations commute with the postcomposition maps $L(\varphi)$ by uniqueness, so $b$ is simplicial; at $k\leq m$ its component obeys $\varepsilon'_k b_k=\beta_k\varepsilon_k$. The mapping property of step 2 makes $b$ the unique map with that property. The same uniqueness applied to identity and composite transformations proves functoriality; applied to $\beta^{-1}$ it proves that $b$ is an isomorphism when $\beta$ is. Applying $\Phi$ to the defining projection equations for $b$ gives exactly the defining equations for the map induced by $\Phi\circ\beta$ between the image coskeleta of step 4, so these maps agree.

source.place: Lemma 0183 (lemma-existence-cosk), naturality of the limit construction and the coskeleton mapping property

proof.text: Take $\mathcal C=\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal E)$ with values in sets. By [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise] (1), presheaf limits are objectwise and evaluation at each $V\in\mathcal E$ preserves finite limits. Apply step 4 to this evaluation functor and step 5 to an arbitrary truncated-presheaf morphism. This gives the coskeleton and induced morphism sectionwise; in particular the canonical coskeletality isomorphism is detected at every $V$.

lean.statement: theorem truncatedCoskeletonFiniteLimits (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (m : ℕ) : ∃ (R : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m ⥤ SimplicialObject C) (ε : R ⋙ SimplicialObject.truncation m ⟶ 𝟭 _), (∀ U, (R.obj U).IsRightKanExtension (ε.app U)) ∧ (∀ U, Nonempty ((Functor.RightExtension.mk (R.obj U) (ε.app U)).IsPointwiseRightKanExtension)) ∧ (∀ U, IsIso (ε.app U)) ∧ (∀ (U U' : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) (β : U ⟶ U') (b : R.obj U ⟶ R.obj U'), (SimplicialObject.truncation m).map b ≫ ε.app U' = ε.app U ≫ β → b = R.map β) ∧ ∀ (D : Type w) [Category.{v'} D] (Φ : C ⥤ D), PreservesFiniteLimits Φ → (∀ U, (R.obj U ⋙ Φ).IsRightKanExtension (Functor.whiskerRight (ε.app U) Φ)) ∧ (∀ (U U' : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) (β : U ⟶ U') (b : R.obj U ⋙ Φ ⟶ R.obj U' ⋙ Φ), (SimplicialObject.truncation m).map b ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (ε.app U') Φ = Functor.whiskerRight (ε.app U) Φ ≫ Functor.whiskerRight β Φ → b = Functor.whiskerRight (R.map β) Φ) ∧ (∀ (K : SimplicialObject C) (c : K ⟶ R.obj ((SimplicialObject.truncation m).obj K)), (SimplicialObject.truncation m).map c ≫ ε.app ((SimplicialObject.truncation m).obj K) = 𝟙 _ → IsIso c → ∀ c' : K ⋙ Φ ⟶ R.obj ((SimplicialObject.truncation m).obj K) ⋙ Φ, (SimplicialObject.truncation m).map c' ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (ε.app ((SimplicialObject.truncation m).obj K)) Φ = 𝟙 _ → IsIso c')
